title: Danh Vo in Conversation with Tom McDonough
captionLocation: Baille Court, Art Gallery of Ontario

sections.title: About
sections.content:
Join artist Danh Vo in conversation with art historian and critic Tom McDonough as they discuss Vo’s exhibition in Galleria Italia at the AGO.

Danh Vo was born in 1975 in Bà Rịa, Vietnam. As a child he fled with his family and settled in Denmark. Vo lives in rural Germany on his studio and farm, Güldenhof. Vo represented Denmark at the Venice Biennale in 2015 and that same year, co-curated Slip of the Tongue at the Punta della Dogana, Venice. In 2013 and 2019, he participated in the International Exhibition of the Biennale. Selected institutional solo exhibitions include the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam (2026); Fondazione Nicola del Roscio, Rome, Italy (2026); M+, Hong Kong (2024–ongoing); Bourse de Commerce, Paris (2023); Mudam Luxembourg (2021); Secession, Vienna (2021); National Museum of Art, Osaka (2020); and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York (2018). He was awarded the Blau Orange Kunstpreis der Deutschen Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken in 2007 and the Hugo Boss Prize in 2012.

Tom McDonough is an art historian, critic and curator whose work focuses on modern and contemporary art, critical theory and visual culture. He is a professor of art history at Binghamton University - State University of New York, where he teaches courses on postwar art, urbanism and the politics of representation. His essays and reviews, published in leading journals and magazines including Artforum, OCTOBER and Texte zur Kunst, combine close analysis of artistic practices with broader questions concerning media, public space, memory and the social conditions of contemporary culture.

For further information see https://ago.ca/events/danh-vo-conversation-tom-mcdonough

Danh Vo: Ships that pass in the night is organized by the Art Gallery of Ontario in collaboration with The Shen Foundation. This presentation is curated by Adam Welch, Carol and Morton Rapp Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, in collaboration with Kitty Scott, Director and Curator, The Shen Foundation.
